## Natural history notes

A native perennial wildflower in the mint family, characterized by slender upright stems, narrow leaves, and small blue to blue-purple flowers with strongly curved stamens that give the blooms their characteristic “bluecurls” appearance. Flatwoods Bluecurls is endemic to Florida and occurs mainly in mesic to scrubby flatwoods of the central and southern peninsula, where it grows in open, sandy habitats maintained by periodic fire. Plants typically reach about 60 cm tall and flower mainly from September through December, with occasional spring blooms. The species was formally described only recently, in 2023, after taxonomic work separated it from closely related Florida bluecurls.
